title: "Science in Oberon"
subtitle: "More than you imagine"

To mark National Science Week 2026, Oberon Citizen Science Network presented a free community event, **"Science in Oberon: More than you imagine"**, at the [Malachi Gilmore Hall](https://malachigilmorehall.com.au) in Oberon on Saturday, 15th August 2026.

::: {.callout-note}
An archived copy of the page used to advertise the 2026 National Science Week event **Science in Oberon: More than you imagine!** is available [here](national-science-week-2026-oberon-archived.html). The links in it may no longer be valid.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Funding acknowledgements"}
This [Inspiring Australia NSW](https://inspiringnsw.org.au) initiative is supported by the Australian Government as part of [National Science Week](https://www.scienceweek.net.au). Oberon Citizen Science Network also gratefully acknowledges support for this event by [Oberon Council](https://www.oberon.nsw.gov.au/Home) through its Section 356 community funding scheme.

::: {layout="[[80, 20]]"}

:::

::: {.aside}
The National Science Week 2026 event in Oberon was held on Saturday 15th August 2026 in the wonderful _art deco_ [Malachi Gilmore Hall](https://malachigilmorehall.com.au) in co-operation with its owners, Lucy and Johnny East. The Malachi Gilmore Hall is an architectural gem that looks like it has just landed from Outer Space, despite being built in 1937.
![The Malachi Gilmore Hall, Oberon](assets/malachi.jpg)
:::


Overall, the event was a great success, with over 90 people attending the morning session of science and technology-related exhibits, and over 60 people attending the afternoon program of talks given by local and visiting speakers.

All aspects of the day were recorded in a series of videos, available via [this YouTube playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLV47W5g3k9QA) or at the individual links below.

## Videos

### Pre-event field trip on 14 August 2026 to observe Southern greater gliders in Gurnang State Forest, about 30kms south or Oberon township, led by Dr Ana Gracanin, ANU Fenner School of Society and Environment

Elevation about 1260 metre above sea level, air temperature 1 degree C, still conditions (it was snowing at this location just 4 days earlier).
